A bodhisattva mahāsattva who is fully endowed with the restraint of the mind attains the three gates of liberation—namely, emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—and this is called being fully endowed with the restraint of the mind."
"Furthermore, young man!

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who is fully endowed with the restraint of the mind attains the four Brahma-abodes—namely, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity—and this is called being fully endowed with the restraint of the mind."
"Furthermore, young man!

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who is fully endowed with the restraint of the mind attains the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path; this is called being fully endowed with the restraint of the mind."
"Furthermore, young man!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva who is fully endowed with the restraint of the mind abides in great compassion, abides in great equanimity, attains the awakening of peace, attains the awakening of cessation, attains benefit, attains dignified conduct, and attains superior practice, this is called being fully endowed with the restraint of the mind."
"Furthermore, young man!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva abandons wrong views and does not associate with wrong views;
cuts off ill-will and does not associate with ill-will;..."
He eliminates stinginess and greed, and does not dwell with stinginess and greed;
he abandons laziness, and does not dwell with laziness;
toward his parents, teachers, and elders, he does not give rise to a mind of flattery, nor a mind of greed, hatred, or delusion, nor does he dwell with them.

Not abandoning the bodhicitta, not abandoning the mind of faith and joy, and completely relinquishing all other faulty thoughts and mental investigations, nor associating with them—this is called being fully endowed with the restraint of the mind.

They skillfully know that all phenomena are like illusions, like dreams, like transformations, like mirages, like echoes, and like shadows and reflections—neither going nor coming. Furthermore, they know suffering as being like a dream; they know non-self as being like a dream; they know impermanence as being like a dream; they know the absence of sentient beings as being like a dream; and they know emptiness as being like a dream. Thus, their minds attain nothing, are without discrimination, are without stagnation or attachment, are without objective grasping, and are without clinging.
"O Youth! This is called the Bodhisattva’s fulfillment of the precept of mental discipline (*manasa-śīla*).

If a Bodhisattva fulfills the dharma of the pure precept of mental discipline, they will remain far removed from all calamities, attain all the inconceivable qualities of the Buddhas, attain the supernormal powers (*abhijñā*) of all Buddhas, and attain the unshakable liberation of mind."
“Young man!
This is called being fully endowed with the restraint of the mind.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
"Listen with single-minded attention and do not let your thoughts be distracted; The mental precept that is taught is pure and stainless.
Having heard the Dharma, give rise to various practices, And you shall be able to swiftly awaken to Bodhi."
If a wise person maintains the restraint of the mind, it is supremely tranquil, vast, and immovable;
this inconceivable and unprecedented state of the Buddha-dharma is called the purity of the mental restraint.
If a wise person maintains the restraint of the mind, the mind attains liberation and remains forever unmoving.
Attaining the supreme concentration that is like a vajra is what is called the purity of mental discipline;

if a wise person can give rise to this, they will preach extensively according to the needs of others for their great benefit and obtain sixty subtle and wondrous tones— this is what is called the purity of mental discipline.

For the wise, mental restraint is supreme; it brings about the thirty-two marks of a great man and the ten powers and all virtues of a Buddha—this is called the teaching of the superior mental restraint.
If the wise maintain this mental restraint, they shall obtain eloquence and fearlessness.
Attaining the supreme, rare, and inconceivable Dharma—this is called the supreme morality of the mind.

If a wise person maintains this morality of the mind, they will attain the four foundations of mindfulness and the bases of psychic power, and further acquire the right efforts, the faculties, and the powers;
this is what is called the already-explained supreme morality of the mind.

If a wise person maintains the restraint of the mind, they can attain the seven factors of enlightenment in purity and also obtain the Noble Eightfold Path; this is what is called the supreme restraint of the mind.
If a wise person maintains the restraint of the mind, they will attain the abiding in the most excellent great equanimity.
And dwelling in great compassion, pure and stainless—this is called the already-explained supreme discipline of mind.
If a wise person maintains the discipline of mind, they will attain peaceful awakening, pure and stainless;
they will attain the various merits of detached awakening—this is what is called the explanation of the supreme discipline of mind.
If a wise person maintains the precept of the mind, They do not dwell with any wrong views;
Constantly not giving rise to ignorance or anger— This is what is called the purity of the mental precept.
If one can be fully endowed with the precept of mental discipline, even for a brief moment, being without flattery or crookedness,
and without deceit or hypocrisy toward parents or teachers— this is what is called the purity of the mental precept.
If a wise person is endowed with the mental precept, they will forever be free from all matters of greed, hatred, and the like.
The qualities of ignorance are likewise all severed; this is what is called the supreme discipline of mind.
If a wise person possesses the discipline of mind, they will never abandon the bodhicitta.
With resolute faith that is never destroyed, this is what is called the supreme discipline of mind.
If a wise person is endowed with restraint of the mind, they remain far removed from all faults and evils and do not dwell with them;
this is what is called the supreme restraint of the mind.
The mind can enter into phenomena that are like illusions, just like dreams, mirages, and the like.
Just like light and shadow, or an echo following a call— this is what is called the supreme discipline of the mind;
knowing that the affairs of suffering are like a dream, as well as impermanence, emptiness, and non-self—
if the mind can understand these things, this is what is called the supreme discipline of the mind.

Knowing there is no sentient being and no life-span, realizing that all causes and conditions revolve like a wheel—coming from nowhere and going nowhere—this is what is called the supreme discipline of the mind.
Seeking after that mind, it cannot be found; it is without conceptualization and without attachment.
Without objective reference and without grasping—this is what has been called the supreme discipline of mind.
Ultimate truth is like a dream; one perceives that even nirvāṇa is likewise so.
If the wise understand the mind in this way, this is what has been called the supreme discipline of mind.
“O Youth! What is called the purity of karma?
To view the three realms of existence as being like a dream, and to feel weary detachment toward them without giving rise to craving—this is called the purity of karma.”
"What is meant by 'transcending objective conditions' (*ālambana*)?
It refers to knowing that the aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and sense bases (*āyatana*) are like illusions and thereby remaining detached from them.
What is meant by 'thoroughly understanding the aggregates'?"
This means realizing that the aggregates (*skandhas*) are like a mirage.
How does one attain the equality of the elements (*dhātus*)?
It means knowing that the elements are equal to a magical creation and thereby relinquishing them.
"How does one eliminate the sense bases?
It means discarding them by regarding the sense bases as being like shadows and reflections.
What is called 'severing craving'?"
It means that regarding all phenomena, there is no objectification.
Why is it called "realizing the patience toward the non-arising [of phenomena]"?
Because one finds nothing to be attained among all phenomena.
"What is meant by 'knowing all karmas'?
It refers to initiating diligence in order to sever all sufferings.
What is meant by 'revealing all causes'?"
It means that the aggregates (skandhas) are like echoes, for they have no arising.
What is meant by "not destroying the fruit"?
It means that karmic fruits are like dreams, and thus there is nothing to be destroyed.
"What is meant by 'directly perceiving all phenomena'?
It means attaining the patience of non-arising (*anutpattika-dharmakṣānti*) regarding all phenomena.
What is meant by 'cultivating and accumulating the path'?"
Because there is nothing to be cultivated regarding any phenomena.
What is meant by "encountering all Buddhas"?
It means being endowed with the ethical conduct of all Buddhas.
"What is meant by 'wisdom that is sharp and keen'?
It refers to having attained the forbearance of the non-arising of all phenomena (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*).
What is meant by 'entering into the inclinations and desires of all sentient beings'?"
It means knowing the differences in the faculties of all sentient beings throughout their successive lifetimes.
What is called "attaining knowledge of phenomena" (dharmajñāna)?
It means that regarding all phenomena, there is nothing to be apprehended.
"What is called the wisdom of unimpeded eloquence?
It is the ability to penetrate the principles of reality as they truly are.
What is called the wisdom that skillfully knows the distinctions between syllables?"
This refers to knowing the distinctions among the three types of linguistic expression.
What is meant by "transcending all things"?
It means awakening to and understanding the non-substantiality of all things.
"What is meant by 'knowing sounds'?
It refers to the wisdom that enters into sounds as being like echoes.
What is meant by 'attaining joy'?"
It means that regarding all phenomena there is nothing to be apprehended; because one is far removed from suffering and affliction, has cast off the heavy burden, and has attained liberation.
"What is meant by 'attaining love and joy'?"
This means causing those who beg to attain joy, because one perceives the benefit at the time of giving.
What is called "the mind being disciplined and upright"?
It means being able to thoroughly understand the Four Noble Truths.
"What is meant by 'upright deportment'?
It refers to the evenness of the body.
What is meant by 'being free from an angry countenance'?"
It means having severed all faults of anger.
What is meant by “the face is always serene”?
It means dwelling in peace and security together with those who maintain virtuous precepts.
"What is meant by 'exquisite speech'?
It refers to speaking to others for the sake of their benefit.
What is meant by 'greeting with kind words'?"
This means that one first says,
"Welcome," and then quickly rises to greet them.
"What is meant by 'not being indolent'?
It means not abandoning diligent exertion.
What is meant by 'revering one's elders and superiors'?"
This means to revere and fear one's elders, regarding them as spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*).
What is meant by "making offerings to one's elders"?
It means attending to and supporting them according to their instructions.
"What is meant by 'being content as soon as one is born'?
It means not delighting in or being attached to any material requisites for life.
What is meant by 'seeking pure dharmas without weariness'?"
It means the gathering of all wholesome dharmas.
What is called "purity of livelihood"?

It means being content with whatever is obtained as appropriate; for if one is not content, one will give rise to flattery, boastfulness, deception, inciting others, and seeking profit through profit—all such matters are completely abandoned.
"What is meant by not abandoning residence in an araṇya? It means not forsaking diligent exertion;

delighting in remote and secluded places, as well as groves, mountain caves, and mountain valleys; loving the Dharma; not associating with householders or renunciants; not being attached to gain and offerings; severing craving and thirst; and because of experiencing the joy of meditative concentration."
"What is meant by 'knowledge of the abodes of each stage'?
It refers to the knowledge of the abode of the fruit of the śrāvaka, the knowledge of the abode of the fruit of the pratyekabuddha, and the knowledge of the abode on the stages of the bodhisattva."
"What is meant by 'mindfulness without forgetfulness'?
It means recollecting impermanence, suffering, emptiness, and non-self.
What is meant by 'attaining skillful knowledge regarding the aggregates'?"
It means knowing the distinctions among the aggregates (skandhas), elements (dhātus), and sense bases (āyatanas) while remaining without apprehension.
What is meant by "realizing the supernormal powers" (abhijñās)?
It means attaining the four bases of power (ṛddhipādas) and being able to manifest transformations.
"What is meant by 'extinguishing all afflictions'?
It refers to the eradication of greed, hatred, and delusion.
What is meant by 'eradicating habitual tendencies'?"
This means that one loathes former ignorant practices and takes no pleasure in the stages of the Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas.
What is called "superior transformative practice"?
It refers to being able to give rise to the powers, fearlessnesses, and four unhindered analytical knowledges of a Tathāgata.
"What is called 'cultivating the cause'?
It refers to severing hatred and attachment.
What is called 'knowing the means of transgression'?"
This means knowing the *prātimokṣa*, knowing the *vinaya*, and knowing the precepts.
What is meant by "severing all remorse and affliction"?
It is the sincere repentance for all transgressions and faults, vowing not to commit them again, and cultivating all wholesome dharmas.
"What is meant by 'severing attachment'?
It is to uproot the branches of craving within the three realms, and to cause unarisen virtues to arise and already arisen virtues not to be lost."
"What is meant by 'transcending all states of existence' (bhava)?
It means that regarding the three realms, one has nothing to apprehend and harbors no further concern; this is called transcending all states of existence."
"What is meant by 'clearly understanding past lives'?
It refers to recollecting and knowing the events of past existences.
What is meant by 'having no doubt regarding the results of karma'?"
This means being free from all views of annihilationism and eternalism.
What is meant by "contemplating the Dharma"?
It means reflecting upon the Dharma as it truly is.
"What is meant by 'cultivating extensive learning'?
It refers to practicing, receiving, and upholding the Śrāvaka-piṭaka, the Pratyekabuddha-piṭaka, and the Bodhisattva-piṭaka.
What is meant by 'attaining swift and sharp wisdom'?"
It means that one contemplates the wisdom of non-arising as being like a dream.
What is meant by "delighting in wisdom"?
It refers to the constant cultivation of wisdom.
"What is called 'penetrating wisdom'?
It is that which gives rise to *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
What is called 'attaining the stage of subjugation'?"
This refers to the training precepts practiced by a bodhisattva.
Why is it said to be "like a mountain"?
It is because one does not abandon the mind of enlightenment (bodhicitta).
"What is meant by 'immovable'?
It refers to non-discrimination, because one is not carried away by afflictions.
What is meant by 'not agitated'?"
This refers to being without discursive thought regarding any signs.
What is called the "sign of non-retrogression"?
It means that one does not lack or diminish any of the six *pāramitās*, and constantly beholds the Buddhas of other lands.
"What is meant by 'producing wholesome dharmas'?
It refers to drawing near to *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
What is meant by 'disgust for and detachment from evil karma'?"
What is meant by "firmly maintaining the prohibitive precepts" is that one does not give rise to further evil.
What is meant by "not engaging in afflictions"?
It is that one does not give rise to ignorance, craving for existence, or hatred.
"What is meant by 'not abandoning the precepts'?
It refers to having faith in cause and effect and revering the Tathāgata.
What is meant by 'discerning the various dhyānas'?"
This refers to knowing the mind and its mental factors, attaining single-mindedness through skillful means.
What is meant by "knowing the inclinations and desires of all sentient beings"?
It refers to knowing the distinctions among their faculties.
"What is called the wisdom that skillfully discriminates the places of birth?
It is the knowledge of the distinctions among the five destinies.
What is called boundless wisdom?"
This refers to the spontaneous knowledge of worldly and world-transcending phenomena.
What is called "knowledge of the sequence of speech"?
It refers to the ability to understand the skillful and esoteric expressions of the Tathāgata.
"What is meant by 'renouncing worldly attachments'?
It refers to leaving the household life through physical and mental detachment.
What is meant by 'not delighting in the three realms'?"
This refers to seeing the three realms as they truly are.
What is called "a mind that is not inferior"?
It means not abandoning the mind; even when entering meditative absorption (*samāpatti*), one does not abandon it.
"What is meant by 'non-attachment toward all phenomena'?
It refers to the relinquishing of craving for all phenomena.
What is meant by 'upholding the true Dharma'?"
Because one protects the Buddha by thus practicing these sūtras, this is called "upholding the true Dharma.
What is meant by "protecting the true Dharma"?
It means subduing all sentient beings who slander the Dharma through the Dharma itself; this is called protecting the Dharma.
"What is meant by 'having faith in the retribution of karma'?
It refers to feeling shame for all evil deeds, becoming weary of them, and cultivating wholesome dharmas.
What is meant by 'knowing the skillful means of the Vinaya'?"
This refers to knowing what constitutes an offense and what does not regarding one's own nature, and knowing what constitutes an offense and what does not regarding the nature of the act.
"What is meant by extinguishing all disputes?
It means abandoning the clamor of the multitude."
"What is meant by 'not being in contradiction'?
It refers to not taking pleasure in any worldly speech.
What is meant by 'the stage of patience'?"
What is called patience is because one endures the afflictions of body and mind.
What is meant by "embracing patience"?
It means being able to completely renounce all coarse and evil speech uttered by others, maintaining patience without diminution.
"What is meant by 'discerning the dharmas'?

It refers to knowing the distinctions among the aggregates (skandha), elements (dhātu), and sense bases (āyatana); knowing the factors conducive to outflow (sāsrava) and the factors conducive to the path of purification (anāsrava); and because one has no attainment regarding those dharmas."
"What is called 'decisive skillful means'?
It refers to the fact that there is nothing whatsoever to be expressed regarding all phenomena.
What is called 'the wisdom that well knows the distinctions between words and meanings'?"
This refers to the thorough penetration of all phenomena.
What is called "skillful wisdom in the production of dharma-words"?
It refers to the teaching of phenomena as they truly are.
"What is called the wisdom that discerns between what is meaningful and what is meaningless?
It is the knowledge that the nature of phenomena neither increases nor decreases.
What is called the wisdom of the past?"
This refers to the wisdom of causes.
What is called the wisdom of the posterior limit?
It refers to the wisdom of conditions.
"What is meant by the 'wisdom of the equality of the three periods of time'?
It refers to the thorough understanding that all phenomena (dharmas) are without distinction, because one abides in the state of non-phenomena."
“What is called the wisdom that knows the distinctions of the three periods of time?
It is the non-apprehension of phenomena in the three periods of time, as well as the absence of mental recollection.
What is called the abiding of the mind?”
This refers to not apprehending [anything] within the mind.
What is called "abiding in the body"?
It refers to the foundation of mindfulness of the body; this is called abiding in the body.
"What is meant by 'guarding dignified conduct' (*īryāpatha*)?
It means that one's dignified conduct is free from confusion.
What is meant by 'not violating dignified conduct'?"
This refers to concealing virtuous deeds.
What is meant by "not discriminating regarding deportment"?
It refers to being free from the desire for and the malicious mind [toward others].
"What is meant by 'the faculties being dignified and beautiful'?
It refers to deliberating upon the course of the Dharma, speaking in accordance with what is taught, knowing the proper timing, and expounding the Dharma as it truly is, according to its reality."
"What is called conventional knowledge (*saṃvṛti-jñāna*)?
Because it skillfully knows dharmas of the past and future, it is called conventional knowledge.
What is called the equanimity of liberation (*vimukti-upekṣā*)?"
This refers to not concealing or being stingy or envious regarding whatever wealth one possesses.
What is meant by "always extending the hand of giving"?
It refers to being well-established in common adherence to the precepts.
"What is meant by 'having no stinginess'?
It refers to giving with a faithful heart until one's resources are exhausted.
What is meant by 'shame' (hrī)?"
What is called "shame" (hrī) is the feeling of being ashamed of various forms of violence and evil.
What is called "moral dread" (apatrāpya)?
It is the feeling of being ashamed of various forms of folly and harm.
"What is meant by 'hating and abandoning the mind of evil'?
It means knowing the dharmas of ignorance and abandoning them so as not to dwell with them.
What is meant by 'not relinquishing the dhūta practices'?"
This refers to having firm resolve that is without regression.
What is meant by "receiving the precept of truthfulness"?
It means acting exactly as one speaks.
"What is meant by 'arousing the practice of joy'?
It refers to reflecting upon the benefit of wholesome dharmas.
What is meant by 'dwelling in proximity to one's elders'?"
This refers to abandoning arrogance and remaining free from the causes of indolence.
What is meant by "subduing arrogance"?
It means that a self cannot be apprehended, because there is no objective basis for grasping.
"What is meant by 'subduing the mind'?
It refers to the wisdom that does not lose the benefit of mindfulness regarding all wholesome dharmas (*śukla-dharma*).
What is meant by 'the mental faculty of uplifting'?"
This is called knowing the fruit of diligence because it does not lose wisdom.
What is called the wisdom of the analytical knowledge of meaning?
It is the thorough penetration of wisdom as it truly is.
"What is meant by 'thoroughly knowing wisdom'?
It refers to knowing mundane phenomena and supramundane phenomena.
What is meant by 'the wisdom that is free from non-wisdom'?"
This refers to being free from grasping and attachment toward phenomena as they truly are.
What is called "the wisdom that enters the mind"?
It refers to the wisdom of non-arising and non-ceasing.
"What is called the skillful wisdom of discerning distinctions?
It is the sharp and penetrating wisdom of differentiation.
What is called the wisdom that knows all speech and sounds?"
This refers to the wisdom that demonstrates the Dharma as it truly is.
What is called "the wisdom that knows locations"?
It refers to entering into the wisdom of reality as it is.
"What is meant by the wisdom of skillful means for determining names and meanings?
It is said to be the act of reverently attending upon all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Śrāvakas.
What is meant by abandoning that which is not meaningful?"
This is called "skillfully entering" because it transcends all states of existence (*bhava*).
What is meant by "associating with virtuous persons and engaging in their activities"?
It refers to attending upon and serving the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Śrāvakas.
"What is meant by 'keeping far from evil persons'?
It means keeping far from those who grasp at a self and those who are indolent.
What is meant by 'cultivating dhyāna and developing supernormal powers'?"
This refers to being free from the thorns of desire while not abandoning the joy of dhyāna.
What is meant by "not clinging to the flavor of dhyāna"?
It means desiring to transcend the three realms.
“What is meant by ‘mastery over supernormal powers’?
It refers to abiding in the five supernormal powers and being able to manifest for others that which is difficult to know within the Buddha-dharma.
What is meant by ‘understanding conventional designations’?”
This is called "understanding that names are not ultimate.
What is meant by "understanding conventional designations"?
It means knowing worldly names, numbers, and syllables.
"What is meant by 'transcending conventional designations'?
It refers to the knowledge that realizes the absence of verbal expression.
What is meant by 'being detached from the world'?"
This refers to first contemplating the faults and evils of the world.
"How does one not delight in fame and profit?
This refers to having a nature of few desires by its very essence.
"What is meant by not being attached to gain and offerings?
It means being free from all covetous seeking and having abandoned evil desires.
What is meant by not giving rise to anger or resentment when hearing others revile or abuse one?"
This refers to understanding the nature of the aggregates (skandhas) and elements (dhātus).
"How is it that one does not give rise to joy upon hearing praise of one's true virtues?
It means concealing one's wholesome qualities and merits, and knowing the faults of gain and honor (lābha-satkāra).
"What is meant by not desiring respect?
It is because one fundamentally understands cause and effect.
What is meant by not harboring resentment when respect is not obtained?"
This refers to not abandoning the mind of meditative concentration.
"How is it that one does not become resentful when insulted?
This refers to observing worldly phenomena and awakening to the law of cause and effect.
"What is meant by not being elated when hearing praise?
It is because one has gone forth from home in search of the wholesome Dharma.
What is meant by having no anxiety or dejection regarding material gains?"
This refers to observing the karma created in the past.
"What is meant by not associating with worldly people?
It means having no desire for the necessities of life."
"What is meant by 'not delighting in dwelling together with renunciants who act contrary to the Dharma'?
It means to associate with those who act in accordance with the Dharma and not to associate with those who act contrary to the Dharma.
What is meant by 'staying far away from places that are not one's proper sphere'?"
This refers to the abandonment of the five hindrances.
What is meant by "dwelling within the sphere of practice"?
It refers to the cultivation of the four foundations of mindfulness.
“What is meant by accomplishing the ritual procedures?
It refers to protecting others.
What is meant by staying far removed from what is not the Dharma?”
It is for the sake of protecting one's own wholesome qualities.
How does one not defile other families?
It means being free from the transgressions associated with intimacy and acquaintance.
"What is meant by 'protecting the Dharma'?
It refers to being fully endowed with the quest for the Dharma and acting in accordance with the Dharma.
What is meant by 'remaining in silent seclusion and speaking little'?"
This refers to attaining the wisdom of quiescence.
What is meant by "skillfulness in question and answer"?
It refers to the wisdom that is able to respond appropriately according to whatever questions are posed.
"What is meant by 'subduing enemies'?
It refers to discerning and revealing the Dharma as it truly is, thereby remaining far removed from grasping and attachment.
What is meant by 'knowing the proper time'?"
This refers to being able to know the years, months, and seasons.
Why does one not associate with the foolish and ignorant?
This refers to seeing the faults of foolish dharmas.
"What is meant by not despising those who are poor and lowly?
It means giving rise to a mind of equanimity toward all sentient beings.
What is meant by swiftly bestowing wealth upon the poor and suffering?"
This means that whenever there are those who beg, one causes them to receive gifts of wealth and gifts of the Dharma.
What is meant by "unimpeded giving toward the impoverished"?
It refers to giving rise to compassion for those sentient beings and relinquishing internal and external things according to their requests.
“How does one rescue those who have broken their precepts?
It means removing the karma of transgressing the precepts and establishing them within pure morality.
What is meant by ‘beneficial matters’?”
It means being able to nurture and sustain sentient beings.
What is called "compassionate wisdom"?
It is being able to perceive the future suffering and afflictions of sentient beings.
"What is meant by 'embracing the Dharma'?
It means being able to cause sentient beings to enter into the Dharma as it truly is.
What is meant by 'renouncing material wealth'?"
This refers to relinquishing the aggregates (skandhas) by bestowing material wealth upon others.
"How does one not engage in accumulation?
This means becoming weary of and detached from the necessities of life, having seen the faults inherent in guarding them.
"What is meant by praising the observance of precepts?
It means knowing well the karmic retribution of observing precepts.
What is meant by censuring the violation of precepts?"
This refers to being well-versed in understanding the faults of violating the precepts.
How does one serve those who uphold the precepts with a mind free from deceit?
It means conceiving the thought that such upholders of the precepts are difficult to encounter.
"What is meant by 'renouncing everything'?
It refers to having wholesome faith and joy.
What is meant by 'supreme faith and sincere entreaty'?"
That which is called seeking happiness for others is for the sake of benefiting sentient beings.
What is meant by "acting according to what one says"?
It refers to being endowed with wholesome faith, such that upon hearing [the teaching], one immediately accepts and practices it.
“What is meant by serving a wise bhikṣu?
It means inquiring about wholesome matters.
What is meant by engaging in discourse with others that gives rise to affection and joy?”
This refers to possessing both realized knowledge (*adhigama-jñāna*) and scriptural knowledge (*śruta-jñāna*).
What is called "knowledge by analogy" (*aupamya-jñāna*)?
It refers to understanding the fundamental and derivative characteristics of phenomena (*dharma-lakṣaṇa*) through the use of analogies.
"What is meant by 'skillfulness regarding the past'?
It refers to the recollection of one's own past lives through extensive learning.
What is meant by 'taking roots of goodness as primary'?"
It is said that this consists in generating superior faith in awakening and further exhorting others to do so.
What is called skillful means?
It is the thorough dedication of all roots of goodness performed through repentance, sympathetic joy, and entreaty.
"What is meant by 'eliminating the signs of existence'?
It refers to observing all phenomena and seeing that all dharmas are like dreams.
What is meant by 'eliminating conceptualization'?"
This refers to being far removed from perverted conceptions.
What is meant by "skillfully observing the characteristics of phenomena"?
It refers to attaining the wisdom of signlessness.
"What is meant by 'skillfully expounding all sutras'?
It refers to being able to manifest parables and past events (itivṛttaka) that clarify the dharmas of the wholesome and the unwholesome.
What is meant by 'discriminating the truths'?"
Once ignorance has been extinguished, name-and-form does not arise.
How is it that one realizes liberation?
It is by attaining the immovable Vajra-samādhi, which is free from conceptual discrimination.
"What is meant by 'speaking only a single word'?
It refers to detesting the heterodox paths and realizing the wisdom of non-arising.
What is meant by 'attaining fearlessness'?"
This refers to knowing the power of the Buddha-dharma.
What is meant by "abiding securely in the precepts"?
It refers to restraining and guarding body and speech through the *prātimokṣa* precepts.
"What is meant by 'entering into samādhi'?
It means being unstained by the three realms.
What is meant by 'attaining wisdom'?"
This refers to having well-attained the wisdom of effortlessness (*anābhoga-jñāna*).
What is meant by "delighting in solitary stillness"?
It means being far removed from the faults of clamor and bustle, and never abandoning secluded, open spaces.
"What is meant by 'delighting in few acquaintances'?
It refers to having few desires and being content.
What is meant by 'an unclouded mind'?"
What is called "entering meditative concentration" is for the purpose of removing all hindrances.
What is called "abandoning all views"?
It is the thorough distancing from views characterized by grasping and attachment.
"What is meant by 'attaining dhāraṇī'?
It refers to displaying, without forgetting, the dharmas as they are seen, exactly as they are.
What is meant by 'attaining the illumination of wisdom'?"
This is called "knowing by way of entering into self-nature.
What is meant by "locus"?
It refers to the locus of the mind.
"What is meant by 'abiding'?
It refers to that which is dwelt upon by faith.
What is meant by 'practice'?"
This refers to abiding in the dharma of practice through faith.
What is called "discriminative wisdom"?
It refers to knowing how to discriminate the path.
"What is meant by 'cause'?
It refers to the fact that ignorance is the cause from which all volitional formations arise.
What is meant by 'correspondence'?"
This refers to the dharmas that should be liberated.
What is meant by "dharmas"?
It refers to the severing of craving.
"What is called the 'gate'?
It refers to the severance of all faults.
What is called the 'path'?"
This refers to the wisdom of impermanence, suffering, emptiness, and non-self.
What is meant by "stages"?
It refers to the ten stages of wishlessness.
"What is meant by 'being far removed from birth'?
It refers to the severance of the phenomena of birth.
What is called the 'ground of wisdom'?"
This is because of what is called "unfailing wisdom.
How does one abandon ignorance?
It is by means of severing delusion.
"How does one abide in wisdom?
It is because wisdom has no place of abiding.
What is called the stage of skillful means?"
This refers to cultivating the thirty-seven factors conducive to enlightenment.
What is called the "sphere of activity of a bodhisattva"?
It refers to practicing the six pāramitās.
"What is meant by associating with virtuous people?
It means drawing near to all Buddhas.
What is meant by distancing oneself from evil people?"
This refers to being free from the heterodox views of grasping at [wrong] perspectives.
What is meant by "that which is spoken by the Tathāgata"?
It means abiding in the power and wisdom of the Tathāgata, because its intrinsic nature is liberation.
"What is called the Buddha-ground?
It is the attainment of all wholesome dharmas.
What is called the wise person’s sympathetic joy?"
This refers to the rejoicing of all Buddhas, śrāvakas, and pratyekabuddhas of the past, future, and present.
Why is it called "that which is reviled by fools"?
This is because all fools are unable to know it.
Why is it that śrāvakas cannot know it?
It is because the Buddha-dharma is inconceivable.
"What is meant by the stage of the non-Buddhists?
It refers to the expedient means of the views and pride of the non-Buddhists.
What is meant by being encompassed by the Tathāgata?"
This is because he is a Great King of Physicians who is difficult to encounter.
How is it that he swiftly attains the ten powers?
It is by means of diligently practicing skillful means.
"What is meant by 'being honored by all the devas'?
It means being able to skillfully produce all forms of happiness.
What is meant by 'the Brahmā King prostrating'?"
This refers to the liberation born from that [source].
What is meant by "the dragon’s prostration"?
It refers to the ability to sever all evil destinies and all [wrong] views.
"What is meant by 'yakṣas rejoicing'?
It means that they obscure all evil realms.
What is meant by 'kiṃnaras praising'?"
This is called "being able to bring about joyful liberation.
What is meant by "Rāhula’s praise"?
It refers to the severing of birth and death.
"What is meant by 'that which is practiced by Bodhisattvas'?
It refers to being able to attain all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*).
What is meant by 'that which is sought by the wise'?"
This means for the sake of attaining the stage of non-retrogression.
What is called "attaining the unsurpassed wealth"?
It refers to being able to attain the fruits of human and celestial rebirth as well as liberation.
"What is called the gift of non-material things?
It is that which can eliminate all diseases of affliction.
What is called the excellent medicine for illness?"
It is said that this is because one extinguishes the afflictions of greed, hatred, and delusion.
What is called the "Treasury of Wisdom"?
It is the constant delight in cultivating wisdom.
"What is meant by 'inexhaustible eloquence'?
It is the wisdom that perceives reality as it truly is.
What is meant by 'being far removed from sorrow'?"
This means knowing that suffering is false and abandoning it, because one has realized there is no self.
"What is meant by 'knowing the three realms'?
It means thoroughly understanding that the three realms are like dreams and illusions."
"What is meant by 'crossing to the other shore by means of a boat or raft'?
It refers to entering parinirvāṇa with faith and joy, by cultivating the wisdom of impermanence, suffering, emptiness, and non-self."
"What is meant by 'the boat for crossing the four currents'?
It refers to the swift attainment of nirvāṇa.
What is meant by 'one who seeks renown'?"
This refers to being able to attain the vast Dharma.
What is meant by "praising and manifesting the merits of the Tathāgata"?
It means to proclaim that he bestows the medicinal medicine of immeasurable meritorious dharmas.
"What is meant by 'praising the fame of the Tathāgata'?
It means speaking of him as the donor who bestows all merit and liberation, for he delights in being a donor.
What is meant by 'praising the ten powers'?"
This means that one is called "the master of the great Dharma-jewel" because of being able to bestow the Dharma that is difficult to obtain.
"What is called the merit of a bodhisattva?
It is said to be the ability to study the dharma of this sūtra’s samādhi.
What is called 'loving-kindness that extinguishes ill-will'?"
This refers to the antidote to ill-will.
What is called "compassion"?
It is the eradication of the suffering and afflictions of all sentient beings.
"What is called 'joy' (muditā)?
It is the arising of gladness toward all sentient beings.
What is called 'equanimity' (upekṣā)?"
This refers to compassion without an object, for it is capable of performing the work of a Buddha.
What is meant by "consoling those of the Mahāyāna"?
It means being able to provide all the Buddha-dharmas in full abundance, according to whatever they seek and desire.
"What is meant by 'setting forth the lion's roar'?
It refers to being able to bring about the supreme Dharma.
What is meant by 'the path of the Buddha’s wisdom'?"
This refers to attaining wholesome dharmas by being without grasping or attachment toward any wholesome dharmas.
What is meant by "liberating all sentient beings"?
It refers to being able to know how to go from this shore to the other shore.
"What is meant by 'attaining the knowledge of all modes' (sarvajñajñāna)?
It refers to the severance of all unwholesome dharmas, and the accumulation of all wholesome dharmas as well as all liberations."
"What is called the 'Garden of the Bodhisattva'?
It is that which enables one to attain joy and personal peace, and likewise brings peace and happiness to all sentient beings.
What is called 'Subduing the Army of Māra'?"
It is said that it is so called because it can obtain all powers and extinguish all afflictions.
What is meant by "the dhāraṇī of peaceful conduct"?
It is so called because it can bring all suffering and hardship to an end.
"What is meant by 'accomplishing auspicious matters'?
It refers to being able to obtain all karmic fruits and rewards.
What is meant by 'warding off enemies'?"
This refers to the severing of all false views and views of grasping.
What is meant by "subduing enemies"?
It refers to subduing all non-Buddhists through the True Dharma.
"How does one attain fearlessness?
It is by being able to skillfully observe and repeatedly cultivate all phenomena.
How does one seek the power of reality as it is?"
This refers to seeking the power of non-perverted dharmas.
What is called the initial characteristic of the eighteen unique qualities (*āveṇika-dharma*)?
It is the performance of all wholesome dharmas.
“How does one adorn the Dharma-body?
It is by attaining the adornment of the thirty-two marks.
How does one delight in liberation?”
This is because it attains what is excellent in the beginning, middle, and end.
Why is it called the beloved eldest son?
Because it is able to obtain the remaining wealth of the Buddhas, who are its fathers.
"What is meant by 'fulfilling the Buddha-wisdom'?
It refers to exclusively cultivating all pure dharmas (*śukla-dharma*).
What is meant by 'not the stage of a Pratyekabuddha'?"
This refers to being able to attain the supreme and boundless Buddha-dharmas.
What is called the "pure mind"?
It is that which is able to sever and eliminate all defilements.
"What is meant by 'purity of body'?
It refers to the extinguishing of all illnesses.
What is meant by 'accomplishing the gates of liberation'?"
Because they contemplate impermanence, suffering, emptiness, non-self, and cessation.
What is meant by "being free from all miscellaneous desires"?
It refers to being able to attain the phrases of the Dharma that are like nectar.
"What is meant by 'being free from hatred'?
It refers to the attainment of great loving-kindness (*maitrī*) and great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*).
What is called 'the ground that is not of delusion'?"
This refers to attaining illumination that accords with reality.
What is called "knowledge derived from scripture" (āgama-jñāna)?
It refers to the knowledge that understands all activities performed within the mundane and supramundane realms.
"What is meant by 'being able to initiate clarity'?
It refers to recollecting only that which leads to all wholesome paths.
What is meant by 'severing ignorance'?"
This means the cessation of all conceptualizations regarding non-virtuous rebirths.
What is called "fulfillment of liberation"?
It refers to the attainment of the Dharma of the Great Sage.
"What is meant by 'the practitioner of dhyāna attaining tranquility and joy'?
It refers to being able to attain joy, bliss, and one-pointedness of mind.
What is meant by 'one who sees with the eye'?"
What is called "seeing the true meaning" is because there is nothing to be seen.
What is called "the manifestation of supernormal powers"?
It is the skillful cultivation of unobstructed dharmas.
"What is called 'the manifestation of the bases of psychic power' (*ṛddhipāda*)?
It refers to being able to attain non-conceptual wisdom regarding all phenomena, because there is no obstruction.
What is called 'the dharani of delighting in hearing'?"
This refers to thoroughly knowing all phenomena, because one is able to proceed toward the equality of nirvāṇa regarding all phenomena.
How does one maintain mindfulness without forgetting?
It means that the intrinsic nature of all objects of attachment is extinguished.
"What is meant by 'the Tathāgata’s sustaining power' (adhiṣṭhāna)?
It refers to the fact that the various merits and wisdoms he brings forth are indestructible.
What is meant by 'the skillful guide through expedient means'?"
This means causing others to proceed toward the great city of peace and happiness.
Why is it called "subtle wisdom like the tip of a hair"?
It is because it is difficult to fathom and know.
"How is it difficult to know and difficult to correspond with?
It is because it has never been attained before.
How is it free from words and letters?"
This means that the path of speech cannot be apprehended.
Why is it called "the sound being difficult to know"?
It is because all phenomena are inconceivable.
"What is meant by 'the wise who are able to know'?
It means knowing that dharmas are priceless jewels.
What is meant by 'having already known what is to be known through the wisdom of subduing'?"
This means acting in accordance with what one says.
What is meant by "knowing few desires"?
It means knowing the faults of many desires.
“What is called ‘valiant diligence’?
It means knowing how not to abandon one’s commitment.
What is called ‘recollection and dhāraṇī’?”
This means that because whatever one does is never lost.
What is meant by "exhausting suffering"?
It means the eradication of greed, hatred, and delusion.
"What is meant by 'all phenomena are unarisen'?
It means the cessation of all consciousness and all aspirations.
What is meant by 'a single utterance being able to know all realms of birth and death'?"
This means that one contemplates all phenomena as being like dreams and illusions, because of non-attachment.
"O Youth! This concludes the explanation of the meaning of the Dharma-gate of three hundred phrases."
"Young man!
This is the Samādhi of the Equality of the Essential Nature of All Dharmas, Free from Proliferation.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke these verses:
“The wisdom of the Buddha-dharma is immeasurable, its exposition inexhaustible;
having extensively expounded all dharmas, one universally attains all merits.
Vast as space, such is the characteristic of this Dharma.”
This is the ultimate treasure; therefore, it is called Vaipulya.
Since the practices of sentient beings are boundless, the teaching of the Dharma is likewise vast.
Because the meaning of the *āgama* is inexhaustible, it is designated as Vaipulya.

When this Dharma was being taught, immeasurable sentient beings all resolved to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*; immeasurable sentient beings attained non-retrogression from bodhi; immeasurable sentient beings resolved to become *pratyekabuddhas*; and immeasurable sentient beings realized the three fruits [of the śrāvaka path].

Furthermore, this trichiliocosm shook in six ways; celestial exquisite fragrances rained down, heavenly flowers were scattered, hundreds of thousands of millions of kinds of celestial music were played, and celestial garments rained from the void, spiraling downward while uttering these words:
"Because these sentient beings have heard this Dharma, they have obtained great and wholesome benefit.

Because these sentient beings have planted roots of goodness under immeasurable Buddhas in the past, they hear this Dharma with joy, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, copy it, and explain it for others; they act as supreme fields of merit for all sentient beings, accomplish the benefit of all sentient beings, and ensure that the lineage of the Buddhas is never severed."
"These sentient beings are certain to be able to serve as the preliminary path to Bodhi; upon hearing this Dharma-gate, they will give rise to practice according to reality.
At that time, the Buddha addressed Ānanda:
"You should receive and uphold this Dharma-gate, read and recite it, receive and uphold it, transcribe it, and explain it extensively for others."
Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
“What should this sutra be named?
How should it be upheld?”
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"This sutra is named 'Entering into Great Compassion'; you should receive and uphold it.
It is also named 'The Samādhi of the Equality of the Essential Nature of All Dharmas and the Absence of Proliferation'; you should receive and uphold it."
Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying, “In accordance with the Buddha’s command, I shall receive and uphold this Dharma-gate.

When this sutra had been spoken, at that time the youth Candraprabha leaped for joy; as did eighty billion nayutas of bodhisattvas, including Ajita-bodhisattva and others, as well as the Elder Ānanda and the fourfold assembly—bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās—the Śuddhāvāsa devas, Brahmā, the Lord of the Sahā World, Śakra-devendra, the Four Heavenly Kings, and all other devas, humans, and asuras. Having heard what the Buddha taught, they rejoiced and practiced accordingly.
